samples.summary: Matching CI by workflow PATH does not make gate 1 "unforgeable": for `pull_request` runs the file at `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is the PULL REQUEST's own copy, so the same actor the comment names as unrestricted can still forge a green "CI" run
samples.evidence: The new doc block (checks.mjs:41-58) and mark-ready.mjs:7-12 justify the change as: "only one file can occupy `.github/workflows/ci.yml`", therefore a run at that path is the real CI. That only rules out a SECOND file. GitHub runs `pull_request`-triggered workflows from the PR's merge commit, i.e. the head branch's version of every workflow file — so an actor who can push a branch to the base repo (precisely the `agent:managed` human PR the comment at checks.mjs:50-52 says "is not restricted") can edit `.github/workflows/ci.yml` itself in the PR to `runs-on: ubuntu-latest / steps: [run: true]`. The resulting run has `name: CI`, `path: .github/workflows/ci.yml`, `conclusion: success`, so `ciConclusion()` returns "success" and mark-ready.mjs:138 (gate 1) reads green with zero tests executed; the hand-off comment mark-ready posts then asserts to the human reviewer that `verify:self`/`verify:integration` are green (mark-ready.mjs:250). The same edit satisfies the new trigger-side clauses (agent-review-panel.yml:166, agent-iterate-ci.yml:54), so the claim that this "closes the arm that INVOKES the agent" is also only true against the second-file variant: a PR can still choose the conclusion of its own ci.yml and thereby choose which `contents: write` arm (panel `fix` vs `agent-iterate-ci`) runs against its branch. The change is an improvement, but the UNFORGEABLE claim in mark-ready.mjs:4-12 and in docs/design/harness-engineering.md ("Gate 1 identifies CI by workflow PATH… anyone able to push a branch") overstates what it buys, and the residual vector is undocumented. A real fix would also require the run's `head_sha` tree to leave `.github/workflows/ci.yml` unmodified relative to the base (or read the required-check contexts enforced by branch protection instead of a workflow run).

samples.summary: `ciRunsFor` prefix-matches on everything before the first `@`, so a workflow file literally named `.github/workflows/ci.yml@x.yml` is counted as a CI run — reopening the "second file claiming to be CI" hole the function exists to close
samples.evidence: `String(r?.path ?? "").split("@")[0] === CI_WORKFLOW_PATH` (checks.mjs:62) accepts any path whose text before the first `@` equals the CI path. `@` is a legal character in a git filename and GitHub picks up any `*.yml` under `.github/workflows/`, so committing `.github/workflows/ci.yml@pwn.yml` (triggered `on: push`, doing nothing) yields a run whose `path` splits to exactly `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and is therefore treated as a CI run by both readers (mark-ready.mjs:138 and set-state.mjs:228). Under the new all-runs rule this cannot turn a red real CI run green, but it does supply a fabricated PASS whenever the real run is absent from the response — e.g. a PR whose base is not `main` (ci.yml only triggers on `pull_request: branches: [main]`), or a head SHA whose real run has fallen outside the un-paginated 100-run window (see the separate finding). The YAML gates are unaffected (they compare `path` exactly), so the exposure is limited to the two script readers. Anchoring the comparison instead (`p === CI_WORKFLOW_PATH || p.startsWith(CI_WORKFLOW_PATH + "@")` — which is what the `@ref` tolerance actually needs) removes it; note the tolerance is speculative anyway, since a same-repo run reports a bare path and a called workflow reports `owner/repo/...@ref`, which this comparison already rejects.

samples.summary: The new "EVERY CI run for the SHA must be green" rule is evaluated over an un-paginated, silently truncated 100-run page, so "every run" can be a subset of the runs that exist
samples.evidence: Gate 1 reads `repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs?head_sha=<sha>&per_page=100` with no `--paginate` (mark-ready.mjs:131; the same call is in set-state.mjs:226) and hands `data.workflow_runs` straight to `ciConclusion`. The Actions API returns runs newest-first, so once a head SHA carries more than 100 runs — trivially arranged by anyone who can push workflow files to the base repo, which is exactly the actor the hardening comment contemplates — the earliest runs, including the real ci.yml run, drop off the page. Most of the time that fails closed (`ciRunsFor` finds nothing → `null` → gate refuses), but combined with the over-broad `@` prefix match above it can fail OPEN: a fabricated `.github/workflows/ci.yml@x.yml` green run stays in the newest 100 while the genuine red CI run is pushed out, and `ciConclusion` reports "success". The old "newest wins" rule had the same input, but the new rule's whole safety argument is that it sees ALL runs, so completeness of the fetch is now load-bearing and should either be paginated or filtered server-side.

samples.summary: `capture-collect.yml` still selects its producer by DISPLAY NAME only — the same forgeable identity this change removes from the other three consumers — and that job holds a cross-repo write token
samples.evidence: The change hardens agent-review-panel.yml, agent-iterate-ci.yml and ci-report.yml with `github.event.workflow_run.path == '.github/workflows/ci.yml'`, and argues docker-publish/publish-ghpage are safe via `head_branch == 'main'` (which I confirmed: both also assert `event == 'push'` and `head_repository == github.repository`, docker-publish.yml:66-72, publish-ghpage.yml:41-47). capture-collect.yml:67-68 was not considered: it triggers on `workflows: ["Agent Review Panel", "Agent Review On-Demand"]` with no path clause and no head_repository/branch clause, and its only job checks out the private store repo with `secrets.EVAL_STORE_TOKEN` (capture-collect.yml:142-146). A file on any branch of the base repo saying `name: Agent Review Panel` therefore drives that job at will. Impact is limited — the collector selects artifacts by name prefix over a time window rather than from the triggering run, and the job runs no PR code — so this is drive-by triggering rather than data injection, but it is the last unhardened instance of the class this PR is closing and it is the one holding a write credential for another repository.
searchedFor: read docker-publish.yml and publish-ghpage.yml job `if:` blocks to verify the diff's 'need no clause' claim
read capture-collect.yml permissions, concurrency and steps

verdict.reason: All quoted evidence checks out. ci.yml is triggered by `pull_request` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:6-10), so GitHub executes the PR head's own copy of the workflow file; a PR that rewrites ci.yml to no-op jobs still yields a run with path `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, name `CI`, conclusion `success`. `ciRunsFor`/`ciConclusion` (checks.mjs:61-89) match only on `path` and nothing verifies that the run's tree left `.github/workflows/**` unmodified relative to base, so mark-ready.mjs:138 (gate 1) reads green with zero tests executed, and mark-ready.mjs:250 then asserts to the human that verify:self/verify:integration are green. The "only one file can occupy it" justification (checks.mjs:54-56, mark-ready.mjs:7-12, docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1904-1916) only rules out the second-file variant, and the actor the comment itself names as unrestricted (`agent:managed` human PR, checks.mjs:50-52) can push to the base repo. The same forgeable pair drives the `contents: write` arms at agent-iterate-ci.yml:52-56 and agent-review-panel.yml:164-169 plus the panel's mutex/concurrency key (agent-review-panel.yml:117), so a PR can choose which pushing arm runs against its branch. I searched scripts/agent and the workflows for any guard on workflow-file modification or for reading branch-protection contexts instead of a run and found none; checks.test.mjs:456-490 pins only the second-file case. Gate 2 (AI panel) and the human merge approval (docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1896-1902) reduce blast radius but are not a hard guard on gate 1's integrity claim, and the required merge contexts are job names inside the same forgeable file. This is a weakened integrity check on the gate that means "the tests passed" — in the security lane, major impact.

finding.summary: The panel/fix triggers still identify CI by display NAME, so the forged-'CI' run the delta defends mark-ready against still drives agent jobs that push commits
finding.evidence: The delta hardens the READ side (mark-ready/set-state now match `.github/workflows/ci.yml` by path) but leaves every TRIGGER side name-based: `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:27-28` (`workflow_run: workflows: ["CI"]`) and `.github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml:20-21` (same). The `ci` job then polls only the triggering run id and exports its conclusion (lines 267-328), which is what `if:` gates the `fix` job at line 1627 — the arm that runs the agent and PUSHES a commit to the PR branch. A second workflow file with `name: CI` (the exact forgery CI_WORKFLOW_PATH's comment describes) therefore still: (a) starts the review panel with an attacker-chosen conclusion, and (b) by concluding `failure`, drives agent-iterate-ci's pushing arm — bypassing the 'CI conclusion is a MUTEX between the two pushing arms' invariant documented in checks.mjs:112-119, and doing so even while the real CI run is red or still in flight. Promotion itself remains gated by mark-ready's path check, so this is agent-invocation/mutex abuse rather than a promotion bypass; I could not fully confirm GitHub's matching behaviour when two workflow files share a `name:`. Fix: add `github.event.workflow_run.path == '.github/workflows/ci.yml'` to the `gate`/`ci` job `if:` in both workflows.
